---
title: Your first scene
description: Start from a reproducible Blender example, then change one parameter.
---

Begin with the public SionnaRT-Bridge vegetation example. It contains an editable scene and stored visual results, so there is a concrete baseline to inspect before running new simulations.

## 1. Select a release and environment

Open the [SionnaRT-Bridge installation guide](https://github.com/fribas001/sionnart-bridge/blob/main/src/sionnart_bridge/README.md) and the matching [validation record](https://github.com/fribas001/sionnart-bridge/blob/main/docs/validation.md). Follow those instructions for the Blender extension and external solver environment.

Record Blender, extension, Python, Sionna RT, Mitsuba and Dr.Jit versions. Do not substitute the environment from a different local experiment without checking compatibility.

## 2. Open a supplied example

Download the scene and supporting files from the [procedural vegetation example](https://github.com/fribas001/sionnart-bridge/tree/main/examples/procedural-vegetation-paths). Check the supplied hashes where available and save a working copy of the Blender file.

Inspect the plant geometry, transmitter, receiver, configured materials and imported paths. Scrub the timeline to understand which scene parameters change.

## 3. Establish a baseline

Use the example’s settings and the installed extension’s documented run controls. Begin with one frame. Confirm scene scale, device placement and radio materials before increasing the workload.

Save the result separately from the supplied example. Record the frame, frequency, antenna settings, enabled interactions, solver limits and seed where supported.

## 4. Change one parameter

Choose one controlled change: vegetation geometry, receiver position, or a material parameter. Keep the remaining settings fixed and solve again.

Compare the same quantity and units. A path-gain map, coherent received power, and a sum of individual path powers answer different questions; label each explicitly.

## 5. Export a compact result

Keep the editable scene and numerical outputs with the experiment. Export a legible still image, a short explanatory animation and a small table of the compared quantities for the website.
